ROOT CAUSE of why four tools independently invented `r.frame`: THE ENGINE SPEAKS TWO DIALECTS. game/src/sim/record.js:51 writes `f: sim.frame` on every trace record, but engine.js:3360 getFrame() returns `{frame, t_ms}`. A tool author who used the harness API first and the trace second would write `r.frame` and be right about half the codebase. tools/journey/jrn06-death.mjs:305 reads `.frame` CORRECTLY for exactly this reason (it is a getFrame() result, not a trace record).

SWEEP RESULT (whole tools tree, not just the named instances): on the ARTIFACT side the `.frame` defect has exactly the three instances R3 named (experience/beat-extract, journey-run, cadence's FLAG_FIELDS) and no more. tools/lib/scenario.mjs:67 `raw.f ?? raw.frame ?? 0` is an AUTHORED input script where 0 is a legitimate default, not a trace read. tools/world/hazard-fire.mjs:114 `r.frame ?? r.f` is backwards but functionally correct (falls through to r.f, then the event spread overrides with e.f).

build-viability REBUILT and DEMONSTRATED on a shadow tree. Shadow B = full tree copy + R3's exact injection `if (!this.__raceGatesEnabled) return null;` at the top of the model closure. BROKEN tree: `verify-model: RACE-INVARIANT (0/22 gated givers moved)`, `per-giver live: 0 modelled, 22 unmodelled`, `static anchors say derived (4/4): CONTRADICTED BY THE RUNNING GATE`, EXIT 20. A plain static walk on the broken tree also REFUSES with exit 20 instead of printing 504/540. SOUND tree: RACE-SENSITIVE (16/22 moved), anchors AGREE, exit 0. R3's tool exited 0 on both.

The key design decision, and it departs from the R3 verdict's letter: R3 asked for a 4th source anchor on `derivedDisposition` being called, saying 'it would have caught this break'. IT WOULD NOT. The `derivedDisposition(` call text is still present under the injected guard. I added the anchor (it catches a different break — the arithmetic being deleted) but labelled it `proves: 'arithmetic-present (NOT arithmetic-reached)'` and asserted that honesty in the self-test. No regex over source can prove a function's arithmetic is REACHED. The closure is --verify-model: a live two-signature differential on getGateDispositions() varying RACE ALONE. A model that returns null cannot move a number, so the break is caught by construction.

SEPARATE PRE-EXISTING CRASH FOUND AND FIXED in build-viability, same defect class (a SHAPE assumption), and it was fatal: bestCaseCtx() set `c.topicsKnown = { has: () => true }`, a one-method duck. gate.js moved topic gates to topicsInclude() (core/topics.js) which ITERATES — `for (const k of it)` — so every --self-test and every full walk on this tree died with `TypeError: it is not iterable` BEFORE round 4 touched the file. Verified pre-existing by git stash. Replaced with grantAll(): a real Set (iterable, .values(), .has()->true) seeded with every topic/flag the quest book gates on.

The staleness check FIRED UNPROMPTED during this run: another agent edited engine.js at 13:24:49 mid-session and the tool refused the attestation it had minted minutes earlier rather than trusting it. The gate IS genuinely race-sensitive on the real tree: 16 of 22 gated givers change their getGateDispositions() number when race goes dunmer->nord with everything else held fixed. 22/22 modelled, so per-giver is not mixed TODAY — but the shape is now reported, and engine.js:4863 returns null without reaction_group so it can become mixed at any time.

THE GATE MY PREDECESSOR INSTALLED WAS DEFEATED BY A RENAME. decoupling's scenarioIsF3 was a regex over the scenario's own text, preceded by an early-return on the scenario NAME. DEMONSTRATED, not reasoned about: I copied cmb-duel-infantry.json, changed ONLY the id and title strings to say f3-boss-arena / boss / champion, and the detector returned TRUE for a trash mob on flat ground. The name shortcut was worse — passing a scenario id beginning "f3" returned true WITHOUT THE FILE BEING READ AT ALL. That detector is the gate deciding whether a 10-POINT bar reports pass, so a rename would have handed back exactly the green round 3 removed.

REBUILT as classifyF3(): F3-ness is decided from WHAT THE SCENARIO ACTUALLY SPAWNS, resolved against shipped statblocks in game/data/combat/enemies plus fog-gate boss names in game/data/world/hearths.json (authorities 1 and 2 from respawn.json's own note on who classifies an entity). Three terms, all falsifiable: exactly one boss-classified spawn; NO non-boss combatants (a boss with adds is F4); at least one attack press. Five-way discrimination demonstrated — trash duel false, THE LIAR false, bare f3-name false, aggro-but-never-swings false, boss-plus-adds false, and the POSITIVE CONTROL (champion_hist_marked alone in a real fight) TRUE. No override flag is offered: an escape hatch on a gate is the gate.

I COMMITTED THE ROUND-3 DEFECT CLASS IN THE CODE WRITTEN TO FIX IT, AND THE CONTROL CAUGHT IT. loadScenario() returns NORMALISED inputs — normaliseInputs (tools/lib/scenario.mjs:71-82) desugars the authored tap sugar into press arrays and deletes the tap key entirely. My first attack check read the authored key and therefore reported cmb-duel-infantry as never pressing an attack, when it taps light nineteen times. It surfaced ONLY because the positive control said no when it should have said yes. A gate that always refuses is worth no more than one that always agrees, and this loop has already made both mistakes.

decoupling.mjs is now IMPORTABLE without side effects (env ES_DECOUPLING_IMPORT_ONLY=1). Importing it previously launched a browser and ran a full 600-step sweep AND wrote the artifact of record as a side effect of the import, so the exported classifier could not be exercised by anyone but the file itself — round 3's complaint about journey-run's inline expressions in another coat. A critic can now check the classifier with no engine, no page, and no risk of overwriting the figure it is checking.

BUILD-VIABILITY, A SECOND REAL DEFECT, and it is the exact shape of round 3's own cross-check finding. The tool prints "0/540 viable" while its summary reports unpassable_gates.quests_blocked = 0 with an empty gates list, and the operator-facing BUILD FAIL banner NEVER FIRES because that banner is gated on that count. Cause: BOTH halves of the roll-up are disposition-only — the first-stop map skips any stop not flagged race_invariant (false for every stop under the derived model), and the quest scan iterates only quests carrying giver.disposition_min. The gate actually blocking one hundred percent of the grid is a REPUTATION gate, invisible to both. A summary field reading 0 while the walk underneath it says 540 is precisely what round 3 charged this tool with when 240 rows were "compared" and none were.

FIXED with stops_blocking_every_signature: an EMPIRICAL, GATE-KIND-AGNOSTIC roll-up over the stops the walk actually recorded, grouped by quest/stage/gate/reason, with the subset that stopped every signature called out. It needs no model, no gate-kind allow-list and no per-kind ceiling arithmetic, so it cannot go blind the way the old block did. The tool now prints: BUILD FAIL — 1 gate stopped ALL 540 signatures, Q-ASSZ-08 [offer] the_imperial_assize reputation 100/112. unpassable_gates also now carries an explicit scope field stating it is disposition-only, so its 0 cannot be misread.

LIVE BUILD FINDING for the build critic, not a tool defect: game/data/quests/faction-imperial-assize.json, quest Q-ASSZ-08 ("The Legate's Seal") sets rank_gate.min_reputation = 112 while the maximum attainable faction reputation is 100. It is unreachable for every one of the 540 character signatures, and it is why build-viability now reports 0/540 viable against a target of 486. This was already true before round 4 touched anything; the tool simply never named it.

BUILD-VIABILITY'S SELF-TEST WAS FAILING ONE CHECK, AND IT WAS FAILING FOR THE RIGHT REASON. The RED control required the no_unpassable_gate failure count to RISE under the unseed-every-giver perturbation. That counter is SATURATED at 540/540 by the Q-ASSZ-08 reputation gate, so no perturbation of the DISPOSITION register can ever raise it. I did NOT relax the check — a perturbation that changes nothing must still fail. I re-pointed it at the population the perturbation actually acts on (givers whose disposition bar stops at least one signature, which moves 0 to 2), and ADDED requirements it did not have: the direction must hold (every giver blocked in the baseline must still be blocked after) and at least one giver must be newly blocked. The saturation is asserted separately as a named fact, so a future reader is not left wondering why the number did not move.

CONCURRENCY, and a gap in the project's boot gate. The engine BROKE TWICE mid-session from other agents landing call sites before their methods: _mapPoiNames missing at about 14:17 (reached via renderer.uiBuild) and _spawnInscriptions missing at about 14:24 (reached via Engine.applyNamedState). Both healed inside a minute. THE PART WORTH CARRYING: tools/harness/boot-check.mjs reported PASS THROUGHOUT BOTH BREAKS, because it constructs the engine and asks the harness a question but never exercises the RENDER path. boot-check is not a sufficient pre-flight for any tool that renders, and decoupling renders by design.

M6 AT ITS SPECIFIED 3600 STEPS COULD NOT BE COMPLETED IN THIS CONTAINER, and the reason is structural rather than incidental. At render rate 60 the sweep's chunk size is round(60/60) = 1, so it steps ONE fixed frame at a time with the renderer live — 3600 separate stepFrames calls each ending in a full SwiftShader render. That is exactly the loop AGENT-PROTOCOL.md documents as never returning, and it cannot be avoided by setting renderRate(0) because the render rate IS the independent variable. The run was left going for over 90 minutes at load 23-33 without finishing its FIRST of four rates.

THE NEW ROLL-UP IS FALSIFIED THREE WAYS ON SHADOW DATA TREES (--data-root, no browser, real tree never touched). (1) REAL TREE: fires, count 1, names Q-ASSZ-08 [offer] the_imperial_assize reputation 100/112, viable 0/540. (2) REPAIR ONLY THAT ONE (112 -> 100): the roll-up MOVES to Q-LEDG-08 the_wet_ledger reputation 100/112 — it is not a constant that has memorised one quest id. (3) REPAIR ALL THREE: count goes to 0, the banner falls silent, and viable goes 0 -> 522 of 540. A check that fires, that moves, and that can go quiet.

IT ALSO DISCRIMINATES rather than firing on any failure at all: on the fully repaired shadow, 18 signatures still FAIL (every dunmer /assimilated combination, blocked by xul-aneekh-speaker requiring disposition 45 in Q-XULA-04) and the blocks-EVERY-signature roll-up correctly stays at 0, because those 18 are not everybody. "Blocks the whole grid" and "blocks somebody" stay distinct.

SYSTEMIC CONTENT DEFECT, quantified for the build critic: exactly three quests in game/data/quests set rank_gate.min_reputation above the attainable ceiling of 100, and they are the SAME quest in each of the three factions — Q-ASSZ-08 (the_imperial_assize), Q-LEDG-08 (the_wet_ledger), Q-XULA-08 (the_xul_aneekh), all rank 7, all min_reputation 112. Repairing all three takes the build from 0/540 playable signatures to 522/540 against a target of 486. I did NOT change game/data; the repair exists only in a scratchpad shadow tree as the control.

build-viability --self-test now PASSES the check that was failing, with the fix demonstrated in its own output: "givers whose disposition bar stops at least one signature: 0 -> 2 (NEW: dyer-sallis, quartermaster-sedd)" plus the new named saturation fact. It is slow, though — see the caveat below.

CAVEAT A TOOL CRITIC SHOULD KNOW BEFORE BUDGETING: build-viability --self-test does not complete inside ten minutes on a loaded box (it boots a browser for the live model attestation on top of the static walk). This is the same complaint R3 filed against decoupling --self-test, which my predecessor capped. build-viability's is NOT capped. I am flagging it rather than capping it blind, because unlike decoupling's the expensive part IS the falsification (the live two-signature differential), not padding — capping it would be the weakening move.
